Rogue-agent disasters become a government planning test.  TBPN report that the Cambridge proposal would ask governments to create firm response plans for theoretical disasters involving rogue agents. One example is a major cyberattack in which a rogue agent takes down the internet and hacks multiple systems.  The proposal’s focus is advance preparation. Governments would be asked to consider how they would respond to a scenario that could disrupt the internet while affecting multiple systems, rather than waiting for a crisis before developing a plan.  The episode presents this as a theoretical disaster, not a specific incident that has already occurred. That framing matters: the proposal is described as a call for government response planning, not as a complete technical solution to rogue-agent threats.  TBPN also mention other theoretical risks, including biosecurity incidents and economic dislocation. However, the episode says the proposal does not yet provide specific solutions for those risks. Its reported contribution is to push governments toward firm plans for severe scenarios before they happen.  The cyberattack example makes the government role concrete. A rogue agent that takes down the internet and hacks multiple systems would create a crisis requiring coordinated preparation. The proposal reportedly asks governments to plan for that kind of disaster in advance, even though the scenario remains theoretical.  What should a firm government response plan cover first when a rogue agent takes down the internet and hacks multiple systems?  api.talkonpoint.app/r/6a362d… #ArtificialIntelligence #Geopolitics #TBPN

13/13 - What does Russia gain?  The different operations make more sense when viewed together.  FE assesses that Russian hybrid activity seeks to weaken NATO’s political cohesion and decision-making, create sustained uncertainty and gradually shift thresholds for what Western states are prepared to tolerate. It also assesses that Russian influence operations seek to increase division and reduce Western support for Ukraine.   Denmark offers several pressure points simultaneously: • Disagreement about Ukraine. • Fear of a wider European war. • Distrust of governments and institutions. • EU and NATO scepticism. • Greenland-Denmark-US tensions. • Baltic maritime security. • The shadow fleet. • Critical infrastructure. • Cyber vulnerability. • And direct encounters between Russian and NATO military forces.  On 24 September 2026, FE warned that Russia is likely to escalate its hybrid war against NATO and the West further in the coming months and assessed a low but increasing risk of limited Russian military attacks against a NATO country.  Forsvarets Efterretningstjeneste fe-ddis.dk/da/nyheder/2026/v…  That is why the language matters. Information warfare has not been replaced by kinetic activity.  The two increasingly exist in the same campaign.  Denmark demonstrates the progression particularly clearly: Cold War active measures → digital influence → cyberespionage → covert media → destructive cyberattack → shadow-fleet pressure → sabotage preparation → military harassment.  It remains hybrid warfare because the instruments are deliberately combined.  But "hybrid" should no longer be mistaken for minor, virtual or non-physical.  Parts of it are now very real indeed.

2/13 - "Hybrid" does not mean harmless  The Danish Defence Intelligence Service, FE/DDIS, now explicitly assesses that Russia is conducting hybrid warfare against NATO and the West.  Its October 2025 assessment defined hybrid warfare as aggressive use of political, economic, informational and military means while remaining below the threshold of armed conflict.  At that point FE rated the threat of sabotage against the Danish Armed Forces HIGH, destructive cyberattack MEDIUM, and military provocations against NATO members HIGH.   This distinction matters.  "Hybrid warfare" is the umbrella. Inside it we can increasingly identify separate operational components: information warfare → cyber/electronic warfare → covert physical action → sabotage → military coercion and kinetic activity.  Calling all of this merely "hybrid activity" can obscure how far some parts of the campaign have escalated and personally I think we should start naming what is happening appropriately.

Reported cases (government data)  In 2024, the FTC’s Consumer Sentinel Network received about 2.6 million fraud reports. Of those, 38% said they lost money (up from 27% in 2023), so on the order of 1 million people reported a financial loss. Reported losses totaled $12.5 billion. In 2025, the FTC received about 3 million fraud reports and $15.9 billion in reported losses. Imposter scams were the most common category; investment scams caused the largest dollar losses ($7.9 billion). The FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center recorded $16.6 billion in reported losses for 2024 and a record $20.9 billion for 2025. Only a fraction of complaints include a confirmed loss, and the FBI notes the figures are incomplete. Survey estimates of actual victims  A 2026 Stop Scams Alliance–Gallup study of more than 5,100 adults found that 6% of U.S. adults (about 15.1 million people) said they were personally scammed out of money in 2025. Estimated total losses were about $68 billion (range roughly $33–114 billion), several times the FTC’s reported figure. Another 4% said someone else in their household was scammed that year. An AP-NORC poll found about 3 in 10 U.S. adults say they have personally lost money or personal information to a scam at some point, and about half know someone who has. 一扇门，开了十多年，直到今天才被真正关上。  很多人习惯把 iOS 视为“铁桶一块”的封闭系统：统一硬件、统一系统、统一更新节奏，再加上严格的代码签名和沙箱机制，似乎天然更安全。但现实再次提醒我们——再严密的城墙，也可能在最底层的地基里埋着隐患。  近日，苹果修复了一个编号为 CVE-2026-20700 的零日漏洞。其特殊之处在于，它影响的不是某个新功能、某个边缘组件，而是 iOS 最核心、最底层的基础设施之一：dyld——动态链接器。而更令人震惊的是，这个问题自 iOS 1.0 时代就已经存在，几乎横跨了整个 iPhone 发展史。  一个影响所有 iOS 版本的“老漏洞” 如果用一个更直观的比喻来理解 dyld，它就像是手机系统里的“门卫”。每一个 App 在启动前，都必须经过它的装载与链接，才能真正运行。它负责将程序所需的动态库加载进内存，并完成必要的安全隔离。  而这次的问题在于：  如果攻击者具备内存写入能力，就可能借助这个漏洞执行任意代码。  苹果在公告中表示，该漏洞由谷歌威胁分析小组（Google Threat Analysis Group）发现，并已经收到报告，确认该漏洞“可能已被用于针对特定目标个体的极其复杂攻击”，影响版本为 iOS 26 之前的系统。  更关键的是，苹果承认该漏洞已在真实环境（in the wild）中被利用，并且很可能是某条完整攻击链（exploit chain）中的一环。  dyld 到底有多关键？ 安全公司 Huntress 的副 CISO Brian Milbier 给了一个形象的比喻：  “把 dyld 想象成你手机的大门门卫。每一个想运行的 App，都必须先经过它，被组装好、并获得启动许可。”  通常情况下，这个“门卫”会验证应用的合法性，并把它放进一个高度隔离的“沙箱”中，确保它无法随意访问用户的隐私数据。  但这次漏洞的问题在于：攻击者可以在安全检查开始之前，就“骗过门卫”，提前拿到一把“万能钥匙”——一旦这把钥匙到手，后果可想而知。  更令人担忧的是，这个 dyld 漏洞并非孤立存在。在 iOS 26.3 更新中，苹果还修复了多项 WebKit 相关漏洞。而攻击者正是将 dyld 与 WebKit 漏洞进行组合利用。  Milbier 表示：“攻击者通过伪造身份绕过浏览器（前门）的防护，再利用 dyld 的漏洞，最终完全控制整栋“建筑”——也就是整台设备。”  这种攻击路径可以实现“零点击”或“单击即中”的入侵方式。所谓“零点击攻击”，就是用户甚至无需点开链接或下载文件，仅仅接收一条恶意内容，就可能被入侵。这类攻击通常会出现在高价值目标场景，比如记者、政要、企业高管等。  十多年潜伏，为何无人察觉？ 可能很多开发者会疑惑：一个存在十多年的漏洞，为什么直到今天才被修复？  答案很现实：底层组件往往稳定、复杂且高度依赖历史兼容性。dyld 属于系统核心路径，任何改动都会牵动成百上千个依赖模块。在安全审计中，业务逻辑层和网络层更容易成为焦点，而这类“系统基础设施”往往因成熟稳定而被低估。  更重要的是，这类漏洞通常不会单独出现，而是隐藏在攻击链中。  Milbier 进一步指出：这种复杂度极高的攻击模式，与商业监控行业开发的漏洞利用技术高度相似。具体来说，就是那些为政府客户提供定向监控能力的私营公司，比如开发出 Pegasus、Predator 等著名间谍软件的厂商。  这些公司通常会：挖掘系统级 0-day 漏洞、组合多漏洞形成完整利用链，或者提供成品攻击工具或服务。从技术复杂度判断，dyld + WebKit 这条攻击链“完全是另一个级别”的存在。  为此，他直言：iOS 26.3 终于关上了一扇已经敞开十多年的门。  其他漏洞情况如何？ 在本次 iOS 和 iPadOS 更新中，苹果还修复了大量其他安全问题，包括：  可导致 root 权限获取的漏洞  敏感用户数据泄露问题  多项内存安全缺陷  不过，苹果明确表示：CVE-2026-20700 是此次更新中唯一确认已被真实利用的漏洞。  除此之外，谷歌研究人员在报告中还提到了两个 2025 年 12 月披露的高危漏洞（CVSS 评分 8.8）：  （1）CVE-2025-14174：存在于 Mac 版 Chrome 的 ANGLE 图形引擎中，属于越界内存访问漏洞，可通过恶意网页触发。  （2）CVE-2025-43529：典型的 use-after-free 漏洞，可导致代码执行。  虽然这两个漏洞不直接属于 iOS，但从时间线与技术细节来看，研究人员显然在关注更大范围的攻击链与浏览器利用路径——哪怕在以安全著称的移动平台，例如越界访问、UAF、任意写入的内存安全问题，依然是现代攻防的主战场。

Specifically, look at NIST SP 800-53 (security controls) and NIST SP 800-37 (Risk Management Framework). • ISO/IEC 27001 & 27002: The international benchmarks for establishing, implementing, and maintaining an Information Security Management System (ISMS). • CIS Critical Security Controls (CIS Top 18): A highly actionable, prioritized set of safeguarding actions to stop today’s most pervasive cyber attacks. 🪟 Cyber Attack Techniques & Vulnerabilities • MITRE ATT&CK Framework: A comprehensive, globally accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) based on real-world observations. • OWASP Top 10 / OWASP LLM Top 10: The definitive guides for web application security flaws and vulnerabilities specific to Large Language Models (essential since you are deploying an agent). • CVE and NVD Databases: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) and the National Vulnerability Database (NVD) provide a live dictionary of publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities. ⚙️ Technical System Hardening • CIS Benchmarks: Over 100 consensus-based configuration guidelines to securely configure operating systems, cloud environments, and software packages. 🚨 Real-Time Threat Intelligence • CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog: A live directory managed by the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency listing vulnerabilities that are actively being exploited in the wild. • ISAC feeds (Information Sharing and Analysis Centers): Sector-specific threat intelligence (e.g., Financial Services ISAC, Health ISAC) that keeps the agent aware of industry-targeted campaigns. ⚖️ Regulatory & Legal Compliance • Regulatory Mandates (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS): Depending on your industry, the agent must use these frameworks as a source to ensure your security posture meets legal data protection requirements.

マルウェア解析の学び方を、空の仮想マシンの準備から最初の解析レポートの作成まで6段階で示した学習の手引き。初学者が最初の週にGhidraを開いて挫折しがちなのは難しさではなく順序の問題で、リバースエンジニアリングは前提知識の連鎖の終盤に置くべきだという主張。  環境構築→基礎知識→静的解析→動的解析→リバースエンジニアリング→検知・報告の順に、各段階の所要期間と次へ進む目安となる到達目標を整理し、週8〜10時間で約6か月の学習計画も添えた構成です。検体の安全な入手と扱い方、解析結果を検知・対応の担当者が使える形にまとめる方法まで扱っており、防御側の学習の進め方を確認する材料として有益な内容。  【要点の整理】  ・第1段階は隔離した解析環境の構築。Defenderと自動更新を無効にしたWindows 10のVMにMandiantのFLARE-VMでツール一式を導入し、通信の模擬などには解析向けLinuxのREMnuxを2台目のVMとして併用。ネットワークはホストオンリーか両VM間の内部ネットワークとし、ブリッジ接続や、検体実行中の実インターネット接続は使わない。なお、VirtualBoxなどのホストオンリーは仕様上ホストとも通信できるため、「VMからホストへ到達できない」という記事の確認基準を満たすのは内部ネットワーク側  ・検体の実行中は共有フォルダー、クリップボード共有、ドラッグ＆ドロップを禁止。検体はパスワード付きアーカイブ（研究者間の慣例はinfected）で扱い、解析VM内でのみ入手してホストには保存しない。新しい検体の前には必ずクリーンなスナップショットへ復元。入手先としてMalwareBazaar、theZoo、vx-underground、『Practical Malware Analysis』の演習用検体を紹介  ・第2段階は、プロセスやDLLの読み込み、永続化の定番箇所などのWindowsの内部構造、PE形式、x86／x64のアセンブリと、逆コンパイル結果を読める程度のC言語。第3段階は検体を実行しない静的解析で、ハッシュ、マジックバイトによる実際のファイル形式、文字列、インポート関数、エントロピーから挙動を予測し、次の動的解析で答え合わせする練習。インポートの組み合わせから、ダウンローダー、ランサムウェア、情報窃取型、パック済みを見分ける読み方も例示  ・第4段階は動的解析。ProcmonやProcess Hacker、Regshot、Autorunsでファイル・レジストリ・プロセスの変化と永続化を観察し、INetSimやFakeNetで外部サービスの応答を模擬してWiresharkで通信を記録。ミューテックスは検知用シグネチャとして有用との指摘。動作が見られない場合は、仮想環境やデバッガーの検知、長時間の待機、起動引数や特定のエクスポート関数の呼び出しが必要な可能性も確認し、回避行動そのものも情報として記録  ・第5段階はGhidraやx64dbgによるリバースエンジニアリングで、到達目標は手動でのパック解除と、指令サーバーのアドレスなどの設定の抽出。第6段階はYARA・Sigmaの検知ルールの作成と、正規のソフトウェアで誤検知しないかの確認、MITRE ATT&CKへの対応付け、報告書の作成  ・報告書は、管理者向けの要約、検体の識別情報、機能の概要、侵害指標、検知ルール、推奨対応の6項目で構成する例を提示。最終段階の到達目標は、その検体を見たことのない人が報告書だけで組織全体を調査できる状態  詳細は以下を参照：  hacklido.com/blog/1665-how-t…  (※可能な範囲でファクトチェックは実施済なものの、元記事の精度依存や速報・要約の性質上漏れもありうるため、正確な情報は一次情報を直接参照のこと)

Windows Search Index (Windows.edb): The forensic artifact that remembers what Windows tried to forget.  This ESE database at C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Search\Data\Applications\Windows\Windows.edb contains full-text indexed content and metadata from documents, emails, and files across the system. What makes it powerful for DFIR? It often retains snippets of deleted file content that was indexed before deletion — content that may no longer exist anywhere else on disk.  The index captures document properties, email fragments, file paths, and partial text content. For insider threat cases, this artifact can reveal what documents an adversary accessed, searched for, or exfiltrated — even if those files were later removed. It maps directly to MITRE ATT&CK techniques T1005 (Data from Local System) and T1114 (Email Collection).  Parse it with tools like WinSearchDBAnalyzer, ESEDatabaseView, or sidr. Look for indexed content related to your investigation timeline, keywords tied to sensitive projects, or evidence of files that no longer exist in allocated space. The Search Index doesn't lie about what was once there.  #DFIR #DigitalForensics

Mostly, yes — and that's the uncomfortable part. The US has never extradited anyone for ransomware, and the countries where these crews actually live — Russia, Iran, North Korea — won't touch them. So the realistic worst case for a hacker is losing access to their crypto wallet, not prison.The one exception is sanctions evasion. North Korea's Lazarus Group launders crypto through mixers, and the US has actually seized wallets and charged people for that. But that's a narrow slice — most ransomware crews aren't sanctioned, so they just keep operating.The real risk isn't law enforcement, it's other criminals. Rival gangs, scammers, or even their own partners will steal their wallets if they get sloppy. That's why they use mixers and layered wallets — not to hide from the FBI, but from each other.  Because the economics flipped. Ransomware-as-a-service means anyone can buy a kit for a few hundred dollars, and the payouts are enormous — a single breach can net millions, while the cost of getting caught is usually just a VPN and a new alias.On the defense side, most companies still run on decades-old software with unpatched vulnerabilities, and identity is the weak link. One stolen password or one compromised employee account can unlock an entire network, which is why social engineering keeps working even when the firewalls don't fail.The asymmetry is brutal: attackers only need to find one way in, defenders have to block every single one. The Fake Job Interview That Cost $625 Million North Korean hackers did not break the code. They got hired to write it.  Ronin Network is a blockchain sidechain built specifically to power Axie Infinity, a play to earn game that grew to nearly 3 million daily players.  Lazarus Group targets an engineer at Sky Mavis, the company behind Axie Infinity, with a fake job offer, luring them into opening a malicious file. That single breach gives the hackers a foothold deep inside Ronin's systems.  March 23, 2022: Using that access, the hackers take control of enough validator nodes to approve fraudulent withdrawals. They drain 173,600 ETH and 25.5 million USDC, worth about $625 million.  March 29, 2022: The theft goes unnoticed for six days, until a user reports they cannot withdraw funds. Only then does Sky Mavis discover the hack.  At the time, it's the largest DeFi hack ever recorded. U.S. officials formally link the attack to Lazarus Group and North Korea the following month.  Law enforcement recovers just over $35 million total in the years after. The rest, and the hackers themselves, are never fully recovered.

Tower has been named on a ransomware leak site, creating a potentially serious security issue for the insurer while leaving a central question unresolved: did attackers actually gain access to its systems or data?  A leak-site post alone does not answer that. Cybercriminal groups use these sites to pressure victims, attract attention and impose deadlines, but their claims can be exaggerated, recycled or based on data obtained from another source. Until Tower validates the post against its own technical evidence, the listing should be treated as an unverified extortion claim rather than proof of compromise.  That distinction matters. A premature public assertion could mislead customers, regulators and business partners, while a slow or overly narrow investigation could allow evidence to disappear. Tower’s immediate task is to establish whether there are corresponding signs of unauthorized identity access, endpoint activity, lateral movement, encryption or unusual data staging and egress.  Ransomware no longer reliably announces itself by locking files and displaying a payment note. Attackers may steal information and move straight to extortion, particularly if encryption would create too much operational noise or trigger an earlier response.  The broader figures underline that shift. Industry data indicates that 77% of Mandiant’s ransomware intrusions in 2025 involved suspected data theft, up from 57% in 2024. Ransomware-related intrusions represented 13% of Mandiant’s incident-response investigations, while extortion appeared in 23% of cases. In other words, the extortion problem is wider than the subset of cases involving conventional ransomware deployment.  Enterprise survey findings point in a similar direction. According to Sophos data from 2025, 49% of organizations affected by ransomware experienced data encryption, while 47% stopped the attack before encryption. That leaves plenty of room for theft, attempted theft or threats based on partial access.  The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, or ENISA, reported that ransomware deployment accounted for 40% of financially motivated cyber events it analyzed in 2025, alongside data theft and extortion activity. A Security Affairs review of the ENISA Threat Landscape 2025 also illustrates why incident classification has become less tidy. Encryption, theft and coercion can occur together, separately or in stages.  So what should Tower look for first? Identity logs may show suspicious authentication, token abuse, unusual administrative actions or access from unexpected infrastructure. Endpoint telemetry could reveal credential dumping, discovery commands, remote-management tools or attempts to disable security controls. Network records may expose lateral movement, connections to unfamiliar external services or large outbound transfers.  Investigators also need to preserve evidence before rebuilding systems or rotating infrastructure too aggressively. NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 provides an established model for incident handling, while the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 places the work across Govern, Detect, Respond and Recover activities. The practical point is simple: containment and evidence preservation need to proceed together.  Threat-group branding should receive similar caution. Qilin was especially prominent on leak sites during 2025, while Akira/REDBIKE and Gunra have also used publication threats. The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s Gunra ransomware advisory describes the group’s use of a dedicated leak site to threaten release of allegedly stolen information. Even so, a criminal group’s logo or victim entry is not independent verification.  insight.tmcnet.com/insight/t…

FBI’s First Cyber Fugitive Captured — DOJ Says ATM Scheme Reached 47 States | Donald, WLT Report  The FBI’s first cyber fugitive is back on American soil, and the case against him reads like a collision between organized crime, computer hacking and terrorism financing.  Anibal Alexander Canelon Aguirre — known by the aliases “Prometheus” and “The Engineer” — appeared in federal court in Nebraska on Friday after being apprehended in Venezuela and transferred to the United States.  Federal prosecutors allege that he helped build an ATM “jackpotting” operation that reached 47 states, Washington, D.C., and several foreign countries. The machines were allegedly infected with malware and forced to spit out cash without debiting a customer’s account.  The Justice Department says Canelon Aguirre, 50, is an alleged leader of Tren de Aragua, the Venezuelan gang President Trump designated a foreign terrorist organization. He was added to the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list in March as the list’s 540th entrant and its first alleged cyber criminal.  He pleaded not guilty at his initial appearance in Omaha and was ordered detained. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.  The indictment accuses Canelon Aguirre of participating in conspiracies involving bank fraud, bank burglary, computer fraud, money laundering and material support for terrorists. The bank-fraud conspiracy charge carries a maximum penalty of 30 years in prison; the money-laundering conspiracy charge carries up to 20 years.  Prosecutors say the crews physically broke into ATMs, installed malware and then remotely triggered unauthorized cash withdrawals. They allege Canelon Aguirre developed a strain called Ploutus that included features designed to hinder analysis and delete itself after an attack.  That technical detail matters. This was far beyond a thief showing up with a stolen bank card.  The government describes an international operation that combined physical access, custom malware, cash crews and laundering networks.  The scale of the larger investigation is enormous. The Justice Department says 120 defendants have been charged in the Nebraska case, with three already sentenced to 78, 78 and 96 months in prison.  Since the terrorist designation, nearly 350 alleged Tren de Aragua members and associates have been charged nationwide.  FBI Director Kash Patel called Canelon Aguirre the tenth Top Ten fugitive captured under President Trump. Patel also said 107 wanted foreign fugitives have been returned from 43 countries during the past 18 months — an increase of more than 90 percent from the previous 18-month period.  Those figures show why cross-border cooperation matters. Criminal networks exploit borders, currencies and digital systems. Law enforcement has to move just as deliberately across those same lines.  The Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned Canelon Aguirre and nine other alleged Tren de Aragua figures and entities two days before his court appearance. Treasury used both transnational-crime and counterterrorism authorities in the action.  Treasury described ATM jackpotting as a key revenue stream for the organization and said stolen cash was moved among members and associates, including through cryptocurrency. As of August 2025, U.S. financial institutions had reported more than 1,500 such attacks and approximately $40.7 million in losses.  The sanctions package also named figures and companies in Mexico and Venezuela that Treasury says supported the network. Any property or interests in property under U.S. jurisdiction are blocked, and U.S. persons are generally prohibited from dealing with the designated targets.  Sanctions are not criminal convictions, and Treasury’s allegations remain distinct from the charges being litigated in Nebraska. Together, however, the two actions show the government attacking the alleged network from both directions: a prosecution aimed at prison time and financial restrictions aimed at the money.  The government’s case still has to survive the courtroom. But the capture itself is a major law-enforcement result: an accused malware engineer tied to an alleged terrorist-financing network is no longer beyond the reach of an American judge.  That is what accountability looks like when the borderless promise of cybercrime finally meets a federal courtroom in Nebraska.  wltreport.com/2026/10/03/fbi…

Last election somebody made $500,000 selling pro-Trump shirts and pro-Kamala shirts at the same time, off the same laptop, on TikTok Shop…  Both sides thought he was one of them  I was running one side of it. One shirt about the Trump shooting did over $200,000 in sales for me. $12,000 a day at the peak, $40,000 in a single week, 60% margin  The midterms are 30 days away. Here's exactly how I'd run it today:  1) Open a TikTok Shop seller account. It's free and you don't need a company to start. If you're doing both sides, each side gets its own store with its own name  2) Connect Printify. They print the shirt after the customer pays and ship it for you. You never buy inventory, so a design that flops costs you nothing  3) Go on Kalodata and search political shirts. It shows you what every product on TikTok Shop is selling. Anything over 1,000 units in the last 30 days is proven. Screenshot the top 10 for each side  4) Upload those screenshots to ChatGPT and ask for "50 short, easy to read phrases for the front of a t-shirt" in that style, for that buyer. Do it once per side  5) Pick the ones you can read in 1 second. The font matters more than anything else on the shirt. Phrases only. No candidate photos, no logos, nobody else's artwork  6) Build it in Canva or Printify's text tool. 30 minutes, not a week  7) List it at $17.97 plus $4.75 shipping. 3-5 colors. Use the cheaper blank, people are buying the words on the front. Your first 3 photos do all the selling, and always add a size chart  8) Post your own videos first. Under 20 seconds, shirt on screen in the first 3. TikTok pushes a seller's own videos early, and nobody wants to promote a product with 0 sales  9) Then mail the shirt free to people who already post for that side and give them 20-30% of every sale. They believe it, so they sell it better than you ever could. About 99% of my sales come from creators like that  10) Launch the day something happens. A debate, a clip, a mugshot. Every hour you wait somebody else has the same shirt up  Who's buying: people in their 40s and 50s. They're the best buyers on TikTok by a mile, they have money, and they're the angriest ones about politics  The one thing that can hurt you: TikTok pays a new shop about 30 days after delivery, and Printify charges you the second a shirt prints. When it takes off you're fronting the printing. Keep $1,000 aside for it  Republican, Democrat, whatever. The checkout button works the same  I'm running a free training where I teach you exactly how to make money as a TikTok Shop seller. Link in bio

Project Meridian and the Future of American Warfare  Dr. Joel Rutkowski Monday, October 5, 2026 Policy Paper  Subject:Evaluation of the Department’s 120-day future-warfare initiative; the problem it addresses; historical precedents from 1940 to 2026; political constraints; conservative principles for execution; and a recommended path to success.  Purpose: To define the problem Project Meridian is meant to solve, review the long American record of similar attempts, identify the Washington mechanisms that have doomed them, and recommend a method that can convert a short study into lasting combat power.  Executive Summary  Project Meridian, announced September 30, 2026, by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, is a 120-day effort to map the trajectory of wars, domains, and technologies from the subsurface to cislunar space and to identify capabilities the United States must discover, develop, and field. It is overseen by Under Secretary and Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael and co-led by Elon Musk, Palmer Luckey, and Newt Gingrich. The promised product is a public report and a classified annex. The Secretary has said the project is not a new strategy or policy. It is a hunt for domains and capabilities.  The project names a real problem. The character of warfare is shifting toward cheap precision, autonomy, electronic attack, and contested logistics, while American planning still leans on small numbers of exquisite platforms, slow acquisition, and industrial depth that no longer exists at the required scale. China and Russia spent the counterinsurgency decades building counters to the precision-strike architecture that once offset Soviet mass. The Department’s own studies have repeatedly asked questions the building already knew how to answer.  The historical record from 1940 to 2026 is not encouraging if Meridian is executed as a branded vision exercise. The efforts that worked—wartime scientific mobilization and the Second Offset—tied a technological bet to a named operational problem, a fiscal theory, and force-wide doctrine. The efforts that failed—peacetime Revolution in Military Affairs rhetoric, Rumsfeld-era transformation, Future Combat Systems, and much of the Third Offset and Replicator experience—produced language, offices, and contractor alignment without enough cancellations, magazines, or trained units.  Washington will not defeat Meridian with a single argument. It will defeat it the usual way: iron-triangle protection of current programs, vendor-shaped requirements, administration-bound branding, classification that blocks oversight, and a refusal to name bill-payers. Two co-leads run firms with large defense books. That fact is not a rumor. It is a political and ethical vulnerability that opponents will not have to invent.  A conservative approach does not reject outside talent. It cages it. Success is not a celebrated rollout. Success is a short list of fielded changes that survive the next two budgets: ranked gaps, killed programs, competitive buys, industrial second sources, and a command that can use the result after the celebrities leave the room.  I. Mandate and Scope  Project Meridian was unveiled during a State of the Force address at Marine Corps Base Quantico. Its stated task is to look years and decades ahead, “ruthlessly map the trajectory of wars, domains and technologies,” and identify “the domains that we must conquer and capabilities we must master.” The geographic and physical sweep is deliberate: under the Earth to beyond the Moon. The clock is 120 days. The audience for the public paper will be Congress, industry, and the force. The audience for the annex will be the people who actually move money and forces.  The initiative sits beside related moves: a new Autonomous Warfare Command, base energy resilience, drone-acquisition reform, reductions in senior headquarters, and a cultural campaign to restore a warrior standard. Those adjoining efforts matter. A futures study with no operational customer becomes a PDF. A command with no honest map of what to buy becomes another headquarters.  What Meridian is not, by the Secretary’s own wording, is a strategy. That is the project’s advertised virtue and its principal design flaw. Capabilities unranked by a theory of victory become a catalog. Catalogs are easy to praise and easy to ignore.  II. Problem Definition  Meridian is not first a technology project. It is an attempt to correct a recurring American failure: the lag between how war is changing and how the United States budgets, organizes, and buys for war.  The first element of the problem is exchange ratio. Cheap one-way drones, massed missiles, mines, electronic attack, and commercial sensing can threaten platforms that take years and billions to replace. A force optimized for a small number of exquisite systems can win the first day and lose the first month. Ukraine and Red Sea fighting did not invent this condition. They advertised it.  The second element is competitive. Precision strike, stealth, satellite navigation, and networked intelligence were the American answer to Soviet numbers. That Second Offset worked because the adversary could not cheaply reproduce it. Peer competitors spent a generation aiming at that exact architecture while the United States fought insurgencies. The result is not mysterious. The old offset is no longer an offset.  The third element is institutional. From the 1940s through much of the Cold War, the American defense establishment often led the technological frontier. That is no longer true in computing, launch, autonomy, and large parts of sensing. The Department is frequently a slow customer of other people’s revolutions. Internal studies tend to ratify existing programs. Services protect platforms. Primes protect production lines. Congress protects districts. Staffs protect last year’s briefing. The Secretary’s rationale for outside co-leads was an admission of this capture: there are “obvious biases and risks to asking ourselves to both ask the questions and answer them.”  The fourth element is conceptual. The United States does not lack lists of emerging domains. It lacks ranked choices. Which gaps would cause failure in a 2028–2035 peer fight in the first thirty days? Which answers can be produced at home or with trusted allies? Which answers merely decorate a slide? “Master every domain” is not an answer. It is a budget request without a ceiling.  Compressed, the problem is this: America still plans as if time, mass, and industrial depth will be on its side, while warfare is moving toward cheap precision, autonomy, electronic attack, and contested logistics across every physical and virtual domain. Meridian exists to force that recognition before the next shock does it for Washington.  III. Literature Review, 1940–2026  The American literature on the next war is long, repetitive, and only occasionally decisive. The useful distinction is not between optimists and pessimists. It is between studies that changed force structure and studies that changed vocabulary.  Wartime mobilization, 1940–1945  The Second World War created the template Meridian is trying to copy in miniature: bring civilian technical talent inside the war machine faster than the services would invent the same tools alone. Vannevar Bush’s Office of Scientific Research and Development and the National Defense Research Committee did that with radar, the proximity fuze, operations research, and the atomic bomb. Bush’s 1945 report, “Science: The Endless Frontier,” argued that postwar security required a standing civilian science base rather than a return to isolated arsenals. Operations research taught a lesson the Department still has to relearn: measure sorties, kill probabilities, and logistics, not slogans.  The wartime model worked because there was a shooting war, Presidential backing, and almost no peacetime acquisition politics. Those conditions expire. Any peacetime imitation that keeps the prestige of Bush’s offices without the discipline of wartime choice will reproduce the prestige and not the result.  First Offset and official futurism, 1945–1960  Eisenhower’s New Look was the first true offset: nuclear weapons and airpower in place of a NATO army that could not match Soviet ground force size. RAND, the Gaither Committee, the Killian technological capabilities panel, and the Sputnik shock produced ARPA in 1958 and a habit of using outside analysts to break service monopoly on the future. Wohlstetter on vulnerability, Brodie on nuclear strategy, and Hitch and McKean on defense economics made future war look calculable.  They also created a vice that never left town. Prediction became a budget weapon. The “missile gap” mixed real vulnerability with partisan inflation. From that decade forward, every futures study has had to answer a question Meridian has not yet answered in public: is this analysis, or is this ammunition?  Systems analysis and the credibility crisis, 1961–1975  McNamara’s systems analysis and Planning-Programming-Budgeting System professionalized choice and alienated the services. Civilian analysts forced explicit tradeoffs. The building treated them as illegitimate. Vietnam then demonstrated that superior sensors and firepower do not automatically produce a political result. The durable lesson is cautionary. Systems analysis can optimize the wrong war. Technology cannot substitute for a coherent political object. The Pentagon will use “the future” to avoid the present.  Net assessment and the Second Offset, 1973–1991  This is the closest successful ancestor of Meridian. Andrew Marshall’s Office of Net Assessment institutionalized long-horizon competitive analysis rather than consensus forecasting. The Second Offset under Harold Brown and William Perry—Assault Breaker, stealth, precision munitions, and the sensing architecture around them—was not a slogan. It was a family of programs aimed at a specific problem: defeating massed Warsaw Pact armor without matching it tank for tank. Soviet writing on a military-technical revolution, American AirLand Battle, and Follow-On Forces Attack turned technology into doctrine. The 1991 Gulf War looked, to many, like validation.  The lesson from this period should govern Meridian. An offset works when the adversary’s advantage is named, the American advantage is one the adversary cannot cheaply copy, and money, doctrine, and training move together. A list of promising technologies is not an offset.  Revolution in Military Affairs, 1991–2001  After the Gulf War the literature inflated. Writers described an information-age revolution that would lift the fog of war. Joint Vision 2010 and 2020 promised dominant maneuver, precision engagement, full-dimensional protection, and focused logistics. John Arquilla and David Ronfeldt’s 1993 essay “Cyberwar is Coming” aged better than most of that literature because it treated organization, not only sensors, as the revolution. The Quadrennial Defense Review, beginning in 1997, was supposed to force strategy-resource alignment and often ratified the status quo instead.  The peacetime lesson was equally clear. Revolution talk multiplies concepts faster than it fields magazines. Services absorb the language and keep the programs.  Transformation and Future Combat Systems, 2001–2009  Donald Rumsfeld’s transformation tried to impose 1990s information-age theory on a department fighting Afghanistan and Iraq. Network-centric warfare and a smaller, faster force collided with occupation, improvised explosives, and industrial attrition. The emblematic wreck was Future Combat Systems. Launched formally in 2003 and canceled in 2009, it consumed on the order of eighteen to twenty billion dollars without fielding a manned vehicle. It bet an entire ground-force architecture on an immature network, a separate radio program, and the hope that information would substitute for armor. Work was spread across more than a hundred congressional districts so the program would be too big to kill. That delayed death. It did not produce vehicles. Secretary Robert Gates canceled the manned vehicles because the wars already underway had voted against the concept. RAND’s after-action was blunt. The intent was largely correct. Execution failed because of immature technology, unrealistic schedules, shifting requirements, and an integration concept that could not be verified until it was too late.  Future Combat Systems is the warning that should sit on Meridian’s first agenda page. A correct vision plus an unhedgeable architecture is how Washington burns a decade.  Third Offset and the return of peer competition, 2014–2018  The Defense Innovation Initiative and Third Offset under Chuck Hagel, Ash Carter, and Robert Work named the right competitors and the right commercial shift: artificial intelligence, autonomy, human-machine teaming, and closer ties to firms outside the traditional primes. RAND later concluded that the effort succeeded more as intellectual change than as an offset in being. Ideas migrated into the 2018 National Defense Strategy. A new family of fielded systems that actually offset Chinese mass did not. Critics called it a technology list in search of a theory of victory. Branding moved doctrine documents and left procurement on the old tracks. When principals left, the name left with them.  Replicator to Meridian, 2023–2026  The Ukraine war reintroduced mass, electronic warfare, and attritable systems as central rather than niche. Replicator promised thousands of all-domain attritable autonomous systems in twenty-four months. It selected real platforms, then under-delivered relative to the slogan, drew congressional fire, and was folded into successor offices. The Department is now attempting a much larger autonomy bet while standing up an Autonomous Warfare Command and launching Project Meridian. The through-line is unchanged. America is not short of imagination. It is short of the capacity to turn imagination into inventory before the enemy does.  IV. Political Hurdles  Meridian must survive a system designed to prevent abrupt choice.  The iron triangle still operates. Services want their core platforms. Industry wants stable production. Members want jobs in district. A study that says stop this line and surge that factory creates immediate losers. Future Combat Systems tried to buy protection by spreading subcontracts. The politics of distribution is not the same thing as the engineering of a force.  The clocks are wrong for long work. Offsets that lasted had unusual continuity. The New Look had Eisenhower. The Second Offset was built across administrations. The Third Offset lost its name when principals left. Replicator lost its name when administrations changed. Meridian is branded with a specific secretary and three famous co-leads. That is rocket fuel and a target.  Authorizers can love a vision. Appropriators fund continuing resolutions, plus-ups, and protections. A 120-day paper does not move money unless it is written to the budget exhibits of the next cycle. The current fight will always raid the future fight. Any recommendation that mortgages near-term munitions, ship repair, or recruiting for a 2035 architecture will be attacked as transformation redux.  Service theology is not a metaphor. The services do not share one map of the domains that must be conquered. A joint ranking will be read as a raid on someone’s top line. Classification will protect sources and hide vendor influence at the same time. The annex will be the document that matters. If Congress cannot see how choices were made, it will not defend them when the losers organize.  Ethics is not a side issue. SpaceX is a major national-security contractor. Anduril already sells autonomous and counter-drone systems to the services. Putting those executives in the chair that defines what the future requires supplies opponents with a conflict-of-interest narrative they do not have to invent. Hearings, inspector-general referrals, and campaign ads can freeze implementation even if the analysis is sound.  Culture-war overlay makes the technical work harder. Meridian launched inside a speech that also prosecuted a fight over standards, personnel, and the press. Allies of the project will treat criticism as disloyalty. Opponents will treat the study as factional. Serious analysis dies in that crossfire. Commercial-technology politics cuts the other way as well. Parts of the artificial-intelligence workforce will resist military use. Export controls, talent, and corporate acceptable-use policies are now part of defense industrial policy. Allies and lawyers will slow counter-space, undersea, and autonomous targeting even when the technology is ready.  V. How Similar Attempts Were Doomed  Washington does not usually kill these projects with a single vote. It kills them with process.  The Gaither-era studies were right that vulnerability mattered and then became partisan ammunition. Useful analysis drowned in gap rhetoric. McNamara’s systems analysis was right that scarcity requires choice and then lost legitimacy when Vietnam discredited the method and the services rejected the messengers. Strategic Defense Initiative research survived; the architecture became a symbol fight. Revolution in Military Affairs language was absorbed by the services, who kept their programs and added adjectives. Rumsfeld’s transformation fought the wrong war with a future-force concept and lost both the present and the future.  Future Combat Systems shows the full sequence. Announce a revolution before a prototype can be measured. Refuse to name what will be stopped. Make the program a personal and service brand. Let integration itself become the untestable bet. Spread work to buy votes, then discover redesign is politically expensive. Allow the current war to consume the future account. Wait for an outsider with no emotional stake to cancel what the building could not cancel itself.  The Third Offset and Replicator show the milder version of the same disease. Name the right problem. Create offices and slogans. Move the intellectual climate. Fail to realign enough investment. Lose the name when principals leave. Fold the remnant into a new acronym and repeat.  The recurring autopsy has seven clauses. Announce a revolution before you can measure a prototype. Refuse to name what you will stop buying. Make the study a personal brand. Let vendors define the future they will sell. Spread work to buy votes, then discover you cannot redesign. Change administrations and orphan the vocabulary. Allow the current war or the current scandal to consume the future account. Meridian is already exposed to all seven. Celebrity co-leads accelerate branding and vendor definition. A 120-day clock accelerates premature architecture. A mandate that refuses strategy encourages a shopping list.  VI. Conservative Principles  A conservative reading is not automatic applause for disruptors and not automatic defense of every legacy platform. It is a set of constraints on power.  Peace through strength means deterrence that makes a peer war irrational. Strength is magazine depth, repair capacity, trained people, and credible reach. It is not a press event. The state should be a demanding customer, not the venture partner of last resort. Private firms should compete to meet requirements. They should not write the requirements in a closed room and then fill them.  Anti-cronyism applies to old primes and new primes alike. Recusal, competition, and test data are conservative tools. Personal admiration for founders is not a procurement system. Fiscal realism requires bill-payers. Every new domain is a claim on future taxpayers. If Meridian cannot identify headquarters, failed programs, excess flags, or gold-plated specifications to cut, it is an expansion project wearing future-war language.  Industrial sovereignty is not nostalgia. A missile that cannot be reloaded, a chip that cannot be packaged, and a propellant that cannot be made on American or allied soil are not capabilities. They are imports with flags painted on them. Civilian control and constitutional war powers still bind. Better weapons do not create a duty to use them. Prepare to win necessary wars. Do not build a machine that needs a war to justify itself.  Humility about prediction is not optional. No 120-day committee knows 2040. The robust approach is options, prototypes, and the ability to scale what survives contact—not a twenty-year architecture frozen before the first live-fire failure. Character still precedes gadgets. Autonomy fails in the rain, in the jam, and in the depot if the force is undisciplined. Conservative military reform starts with standards and ends with tools, not the reverse. Authority should sit with commands that fight, not with a standing court of futurists above the services.  VII. Advantages and Risks  The case for Meridian is real. Institutional self-study is captured. A time box is better than an eternal roadmap. The project is at least rhetorically coupled to an operational command and to base and supply-chain resilience rather than floating as an orphan paper. It pulls people who have scaled hardware, launch, and autonomous systems, which the Department is short of. The geographic scope matches the actual battlefield: subsurface, spectrum, space, and autonomy, not only tanks and fighters. A public-plus-classified split can inform industry without dumping every vulnerability into the open. If the work is used to terminate low-yield programs, it can increase combat power per dollar.  The case against is equally real. Two co-leads run firms with large and growing defense books. One hundred twenty days against unbounded geography invites a taxonomy rather than an industrial plan. Refusing strategy leaves no theory of victory against which to rank tools. None of the co-leads is a career joint warfighter. Logistics, law, coalitions, and command will be underweighted unless forced into the room. Political branding makes a bipartisan afterlife unlikely. Autonomy-heavy answers can ignore munitions plants, shipyards, foundries, and people. Classification can launder vendor preferences. Washington can applaud a winter rollout and fund the old program in the spring.  VIII. Recommended Course of Action  Success is not a celebrated report. Success is a short list of fielded changes that survive the next two budgets.  The mission should be restated in operational language. Within 120 days, identify the six to eight capability gaps that would cause the United States to lose a 2028–2035 peer fight in the first thirty days, and specify what to buy, what to kill, and what to manufacture at home or with trusted allies to close those gaps. If Meridian maps every domain from the subsurface to cislunar space and ranks none of them, it has already failed.  Politics-proof process has to be installed in the first week. There should be written recusals for any matter touching a co-lead’s firm above a hard dollar threshold. An ethics official or inspector-general observer should be in the room. A red team with no commercial stake should have a duty to record classified dissent. No recommendation should be valid unless it names a bill-payer. A public method paper should let Congress audit the process even when it cannot see the annex. This is not courtesy. It is how the project denies opponents an easy kill.  The working parts of past successes should be taken without apology. From the Second Offset, take a concrete operational problem rather than a cloud of technologies. From net assessment, take the competitor’s system as the object of study rather than American fashion. From Bush’s wartime offices, take civilian speed and then hand products to uniformed commands. From Gates and Future Combat Systems, keep an outsider with authority to cancel, and do it before sunk-cost politics mature.  The 120 days should produce three products, not one vision. The first is a threat-payoff account: adversary actions that stop American power projection, and American responses that change the cost-exchange ratio. No technology appears unless it maps to that account. The second is industrial math: units per month, cost per effect, test status, second-source potential, and dependence on rare earths and energetics. “Exists as a demo” is not a recommendation. The third is a decision package written for the budget cycle: new starts, plus-ups, terminations, and the authorities an autonomous-warfare command actually needs. Keynote language does not move appropriations.  The output must have a permanent customer. It should go to the Secretary and Deputy, to the new command, to acquisition leadership, and to the four congressional defense committees. Then the celebrity panel should dissolve. Standing vision boards become lobby platforms.  The fight with Washington has to be sequenced. Brief both parties’ defense leadership before the public

군사시설에 설치된 CCTV가 단순한 감시카메라라고 생각하면 안 된다. 촬영 영상 자체가 군사정보가 될 수 있고, 네트워크에 연결된 장비라면 취약점 하나도 보안 문제로 이어질 수 있다.  그런데 우리 군에서 최근 5년간 도입됐거나 운용 중인 중국산 CCTV가 확인된 것만 약 1,070대다. 육군 약 510대, 공군·해군 약 560대 규모다. 특히 ‘하이크비전’과 ‘다후아’는 미국에서 국가안보 우려를 이유로 규제 대상에 포함된 업체다.   더 황당한 건 2024년 전방부대 등에 설치된 중국산 CCTV 약 1,300대가 합동점검에서 발견돼 전량 철거된 전례까지 있었다는 점이다. 당시 해당 장비가 중국의 특정 서버와 연결돼 영상이 외부로 유출될 가능성이 있다고 군이 판단했다.   지금 “현재까지 특이사항이 없다”는 말만 반복할 게 아니다.  군사시설에 어떤 장비가 들어와 있는지, 제조사·부품·펌웨어·서버 연결 구조까지 전수조사하고 문제가 있다면 즉시 교체해야 한다.  안보 장비는 싸다고 들여놓고 나중에 보안부터 걱정하는 방식이어서는 안 된다.  군부대 CCTV는 화질보다 보안이 먼저다. 감시해야 할 군사시설이 오히려 카메라에게 감시당하는 상황은 없어야 한다.

같은 질문을 많이 주셔서 이곳을 통해 간단히 정리해 드립니다.  ---  신한은행 공격에서 ARTEX를 활용한 흔적이 확인된 것은 맞습니다. 다만 이것이 곧 AI가 스스로 공격 대상을 선정하고, 자율적으로 은행을 해킹했다는 의미는 아닙니다.  현재까지는 전체 공격 과정에서 ARTEX가 어느 단계부터 어느 단계까지 활용됐는지, 그리고 사람과 AI가 각각 어떤 역할을 담당했는지도 명확히 확인되지 않았습니다.  또한 ARTEX는 특정 LLM에 종속된 도구가 아니라, 사용자가 원하는 LLM을 연결해 활용할 수 있는 구조입니다.  따라서 이번 사건을 곧바로 중국산 AI나 중국산 LLM의 문제로 연결하고, 이를 전제로 대응책을 논의하는 것 역시 방향을 잘못 잡은 것이라고 봅니다.  지금 필요한 것은 중국산 AI가 공격했다는 식의 성급한 결론이 아닙니다. AI를 활용한 취약점 분석 도구가 빠른 속도로 대중화되고, 공격자 역시 이러한 도구를 손쉽게 활용할 수 있게 되는 시대에 우리가 어떻게 대응해야 할지를 논의하는 것이 훨씬 중요합니다.  PS. 끝으로, 현재 언론에서 함께 거론되고 있는 은행 관련 사례들 가운데에는 ARTEX나 AI와는 무관한 사례도 섞여 있습니다. 각각의 사건을 구분해서 볼 필요가 있습니다.

[신한·KB·하나·부산은행 해킹, 구조와 해결책]  AI가 새로운 구멍을 만든 게 아닙니다. 외부에 열린 업무 시스템에서 "이 사람이 이 고객 정보를 볼 권한이 있는가"를 서버가 제대로 확인했는지가 핵심입니다.  ■ 확인된 사실 (10월 4일까지 보도 기준)  - 신한은행: 대출모집인용 조회 서비스에서 고객 약 2만5천 명 유출 - KB국민은행: 직원용 모바일 업무지원 시스템에서 고객 119명 유출 - 하나은행: 영업지원 시스템에서 고객 89명 유출. 신한 사고 이후 자체 점검에서 발견 - 부산은행: 직원용 모바일 영업지원 시스템에서 외주 개발직원 11명 정보 유출 - 우리은행·농협: 같은 방식의 공격을 받았지만 유출 없음 - 제2금융권(예가람저축은행, 현대캐피탈)에서도 유출 보도 - 금융보안원: 동일 공격 IP로 여러 금융사 침입 시도, 해외 프록시로 IP를 계속 바꿈 - 공격 관련 서버의 HTML 타이틀에서 중국어로 "ARTEX 자율 침투테스트 콘솔"을 뜻하는 문자열 발견  ■ 아직 확인되지 않은 것  - ARTEX가 실제 공격에서 어디까지 관여했는지 - 동일 세력인지, 금융사별 침입 경로가 같은지 - 모든 사고가 같은 취약점인지 (크리덴셜 스터핑이라는 지적도 있음) - 공격자 국적 (중국어 문자열만으로는 확정할 수 없음) - 우리은행·농협이 막아낸 이유 - 여러 금융사가 같은 솔루션이나 개발사를 썼는지  ■ 확인된 사실이 보여주는 구조  1. 공격자는 고객용 채널이 아니라 업무용 시스템을 골랐습니다 직원과 모집인이 지점 밖에서 써야 하니 외부에서 접속됩니다. 그런데 은행 측도 "고객이 주로 사용하는 서비스에 더 신경 썼던 것은 사실"이라고 인정했습니다. 외부에 열려 있지만 보안 우선순위는 뒤였던 영역입니다.  2. 탐지가 늦었습니다 하나은행은 공격이 진행되는 중이 아니라, 신한 사고 이후 자체 점검에서 유출을 발견했습니다.  3. 막을 수 없는 공격이 아니었습니다 우리은행과 농협은 같은 방식의 공격을 받고도 유출이 없었습니다.  4. 공격은 자동화돼 있었습니다 동일 IP로 여러 금융사를 시도했고, IP를 계속 바꿨습니다. 자동화는 확인된 사실이고, 그 안에서 AI가 맡은 역할은 아직 모릅니다.  ■ 핵심 개념: 인증과 인가는 다릅니다  인증은 "누구인가"를 확인합니다. 인가는 "이 사람이 이 데이터에 이 작업을 해도 되는가"를 확인합니다.  모집인이 로그인했다는 것은 신원 확인일 뿐입니다. 그 모집인이 요청한 고객의 정보를 볼 권한이 있는지는 서버가 요청마다 따로 확인해야 합니다. 앱 화면에서 버튼을 숨기는 것으로는 부족합니다.  고객번호 같은 요청값만 바꿔 다른 사람 정보를 조회할 수 있다면 BOLA(객체 단위 인가 취약점)입니다. OWASP API Security Top 10의 1번 항목입니다.  ■ 점검해야 할 질문  외주 개발이나 체크리스트 감사를 이번 사고의 원인으로 확정할 근거는 아직 없습니다. 대신 이 질문에는 답할 수 있어야 합니다.  - 객체 단위 인가 요구사항이 설계와 계약에 들어갔는가 - 권한 없는 계정으로 조회·수정·다운로드를 시도하는 검수를 했는가 - 담당자가 바뀐 뒤에도 정책과 테스트가 유지됐는가 - 점검에서 찾은 취약점이 실제로 고쳐졌고, 다음 배포에서 재발하지 않았는가  "점검했다"는 기록과 "권한 없는 접근이 차단된다"는 검증은 다릅니다.  ■ 해결책  [레이어 1] 즉시 조치 - DNS·인증서·실제 트래픽 기준으로 외부 노출 자산과 API 목록 확인 - 사용하지 않는 API와 불필요한 외부 접근 차단 - 민감정보를 반환하는 경로의 인증·세션 검증 점검 - 계정·세션·단말·IP를 함께 써서 조회량 제한, 짧은 시간에 여러 고객을 조회하는 행위 탐지 - 직원·모집인 계정에도 MFA 적용 - 침해 의심 계정의 세션·토큰 회수, 관련 로그 보존 - 업무에 필요 없는 주민번호 같은 정보는 응답에서 제외  조회 제한과 탐지는 피해를 줄이는 장치입니다. 인가 검증을 대신하지 못합니다.  [레이어 2] 설계와 배포 서버는 모든 API에서 "요청자 → 대상 고객 → 허용된 업무 → 허용된 작업"을 확인해야 합니다. OPA·Cedar 같은 정책 엔진은 선택지일 뿐이고, 핵심은 모든 요청이 정책 판단을 반드시 거치는 것입니다.  배포 전 테스트 - 권한 있는 계정은 필요한 업무를 할 수 있음 - 권한 없는 계정은 다른 고객 정보를 조회·수정·다운로드할 수 없음 - 권한을 회수하면 기존 세션에서도 차단됨 - 목록·검색·일괄 조회에도 같은 정책이 적용됨  인가 테스트가 실패하면 배포를 막아야 합니다. UUID 같은 비순차 ID는 보조책입니다.  모바일 업무 앱은 등록 단말, VPN·ZTNA, 클라이언트 인증서(mTLS), 앱 무결성 검증으로 접속 경로를 좁혀야 합니다. 단, 단말과 계정은 탈취될 수 있습니다. 접속 통제와 서버 인가는 둘 다 필요합니다. API 주소와 요청 형식은 공격자가 알아낸다는 전제로 설계하고, 하드코딩된 비밀키는 제거해야 합니다.  [레이어 3] 운영 - 배포마다 인가 회귀 테스트 - 계정별 업무 특성과 조회 대상·조회량을 함께 분석 - 탐지된 침해지표를 과거 로그와 대조 - 금융사 간 위협정보 공유 - 탐지 후 세션 회수·접근 제한·조사까지 하나의 절차로 연결  AI 침투테스트 도구는 보조 수단입니다. 어떤 모집인이 어떤 고객을 담당하는지 모르는 도구만으로는 인가 검증을 끝낼 수 없습니다.  [레이어 4] 기업 내부 AI  ① 직원이 외부 AI를 쓸 때 - 고객정보·소스코드 입력 통제 - 허용 서비스 지정, DLP, 계약상 보관·학습 조건 확인  ② 자체 AI 앱 - RAG 검색 단계부터 사용자에게 허용된 문서만 제공 - 입력·출력 필터로 접근 통제를 대신하지 않음  ③ AI Agent - 전용 ID, 최소 권한, 짧은 수명 토큰 - 허용 도구·작업·외부 전송 대상 제한 - 고위험 작업은 사람 승인 - 도구 호출과 실행 결과 감사 로그  에이전트 권한은 서비스 계정 관리와 같은 문제입니다. AD에서 서비스 계정에 Domain Admin을 주고 비밀번호를 몇 년씩 안 바꾸던 패턴이 에이전트에서 반복되면 안 됩니다. gMSA처럼 자격증명을 자동으로 바꾸고, PAM처럼 필요한 순간에만 권한을 주고(JIT), 관리자 계정처럼 권한을 정기적으로 재인증해야 합니다.  여기에 하나가 더 붙습니다. 에이전트는 외부 문서나 도구 응답에 숨은 지시를 따라, 정상적으로 받은 권한을 잘못 쓸 수 있습니다. 계정 권한뿐 아니라 실행할 수 있는 작업 범위까지 통제해야 합니다.  [레이어 5] 거버넌스 - 계약·검수에 인가 요구사항과 테스트 통과 증빙 포함 - 외부 노출 API 중 인가 테스트가 적용된 비율 관리 - 미조치 취약점과 재발 여부 추적 - 외주 인력 투입·철수 때 계정과 권한 발급·회수 - 운영 환경의 불필요한 개인정보·테스트 데이터 정리 - 여러 금융사가 같은 솔루션·개발사를 썼다면 공급망 전체 점검  금융당국은 외부 노출 자산 파악, 체크리스트 기반 자체 점검, 위협정보 공유를 지시했습니다. 긴급 조치로는 맞는 방향입니다. 다만 체크리스트는 출발점입니다. 최종 확인 대상은 제출된 문서가 아니라, 실제로 차단되는 권한 없는 접근입니다.  ■ 요약  AI는 공격의 속도와 규모를 키웠지만, 뚫린 곳은 오래된 기본기였습니다. 같은 공격을 막은 은행이 있었다는 건, 막을 수 없는 공격이 아니었다는 뜻입니다. "로그인한 사람이 이 고객 정보를 볼 권한이 있는가"를 서버에서 확인하고, 그 검증이 배포 이후에도 유지되는지 계속 테스트해야 합니다.  출처: 국민일보, 뉴스핌, 데일리시큐, 헤럴드경제, 인사이트코리아, SBS, YTN, EBN 보도 종합  #AI해킹 #ARTEX #금융보안 #API보안 #사이버보안 piped.video/watch?v=4eoyIUlo… #AI해킹 #ARTEX #금융보안 #API보안 #사이버보안
국산제품 사용때문에 많은 기관에서 네트워크 장비인 다산장비를 많이 쓰고  그 다산장비의 취약점 자체가 아직도 조치되지않았습니다.  취약점이 백도어로 누구나 망접속이 되는 문제입니다.  선거조작은 팩트입니다.

AI가 해킹을 강력하게 만드는 이유는 인간에게  귀찮고 오래 걸리던 취약점 탐색과 반복 작업을  자동화하기 때문이다.  그렇다면 AI를 막는 것도 결국 AI여야 한다.  젠슨 황이 오픈 모델을 강조하는 이유도 여기에 있다.   하나의 강력한 공격 AI에 더 강력한 AI 하나로  맞서는 게 아니라 저렴한 오픈 모델 수천 개를  방어 에이전트로 배치하는 것.  AI vs AI가 아니라 AI vs AI의 군집  공격의 비용이 0에 가까워진다면 방어의 비용  역시 0에 가까워져야 한다.

틱톡으로 월 300만원 벌고 느낀점  처음에 틱톡 그거 돈 되겠어? 유튜브나 열심히 하면 되는거 아닌가?  나또한 그랬고 이렇게 생각하는 분들 많을텐데 유튜브 숏츠 운영하고 있다면 틱톡도 한번 해보길 권장드림  9월 틱톡 예상 리워드는 채널 다 합쳐서 300만원인데 직접 운영하면서 느낀점 몇개 풀어보겠음  1. 내가 만든 영상 하나를 유튜브에만 올리기는 아깝다  영상 하나 만들려고 소재 찾고 대본 쓰고 편집까지 했는데 유튜브에 올리고 끝내면 기회도 거기서 끝임  같은 내 영상이라도 플랫폼마다 반응이 다르고 유튜브에서는 아쉬웠던 영상이 틱톡에서 반응 올수도 있음  물론 플랫폼별 수익화 조건에 맞게 올려야하지만 이미 만든 내 컨텐츠를 다른 플랫폼에서도 시험해보는건 해볼만한 일이라고 생각함  2. 조회수만 보고 수익을 예상하면 안됨  첨부한 내 9월 화면을 보면 기본 리워드보다 추가 리워드랑 지역별 인센티브가 훨씬 크게 잡혀있음  두 화면 합쳐서 지역별 인센티브만 약 879달러 전체 예상 리워드의 거의 절반임  그래서 틱톡 조회수 얼마면 돈 얼마 나온다? 이렇게 단순하게 계산하기는 어려움  내가 실제로 어떤 리워드를 받고 있는지 대시보드를 봐야함 이번달 잘 나왔다고 다음달도 똑같이 나온다는 보장은 없음  3. 영상 만드는것만큼 원본 지키는것도 일이더라  이건 운영하기 전에는 생각 못했음  내 영상 그대로 가져가는 계정들 신고하는것도 일인데 오히려 내 원본 영상에 역으로 신고가 들어와서 리워드가 묶이는 경우까지 있었음  영상 열심히 만들어서 올렸다고 끝이 아님 내 컨텐츠가 어디서 어떻게 돌아다니는지도 체크해야함  4. 편집 자료는 지우지말고 남겨두자  실제로 리워드 자격 상실 떴던 영상들 편집 타임라인이랑 파일 생성 일시 같은 증빙 자료 제출해서 복구했음  억울하다고 말로만 설명하는것보다 내가 직접 만들었다는 자료를 보여주는게 중요했음  문제 생기고 뒤늦게 자료 찾느라 에너지 쓰지말고 처음부터 편집 프로젝트랑 원본 파일은 챙겨두길 추천함 물론 이 자료만 내면 무조건 복구된다는 뜻은 아님..ㅠㅠ  결론은 틱톡이 무조건 쉽다는 이야기가 아니라 수익화 조건 채우는것도 힘들고 불펌 대응이나 자격 문제로 시간 뺏기는 일도 있음  근데 내가 이미 유튜브 컨텐츠를 만들고 있다면 틱톡 그거 돈 되겠어? 하고 넘기기에는 아까운 기회라고 생각함  내가 만든 컨텐츠가 돈을 벌어올 수 있는 출구를 하나 더 만들어보자 해보고 판단해도 늦지 않음

주식으로 5억을 벌었다는 현대차 직원의 방법은 생각보다 심심합니다.  단타 안 하고, 개별 종목도 안 사고, 코스피·코스닥 지수만 삽니다. 지수가 고점보다 20% 빠지면 현금 절반, 거기서 10% 더 빠지면 나머지를 넣고, 30% 오르면 전부 팝니다. 그 사이엔 뉴스를 안 보고 회사 일만 합니다.  제가 보기에 이 방법에서 제일 어려운 건 계산이 아니라 기다리는 겁니다. 20% 빠질 때까지 현금을 손도 안 대고 들고 있어야 하고, 넣은 뒤엔 더 빠져도 뉴스를 꺼야 합니다. 그리고 "기다리면 시장은 무조건 회복한다"는 전제가 깔려 있어서, 몇 년씩 안 돌아오는 하락장을 만나면 같은 규칙도 다르게 끝납니다.  결국 5억을 만든 건 규칙보다, 월급으로 현금을 계속 채우면서 아무것도 안 하는 시간을 버틴 쪽입니다.

📊 10/4 통합 브리핑  FortiMail은 패치 없이 기한이 오늘이다. NetScaler는 패치해도 웹셸이 남고, Cisco SD-WAN은 어제 이미 기한이 지났다. AI 이야기는 두껍지만, 오늘 리스크는 여전히 경계면이다.  —— 오늘 먼저 ——  ① 🔴 Fortinet FortiMail — 패치 없음, KEV 기한 오늘(10/4) CVE-2026-104286 CVSS 9.8. path traversal+NULL → 비인증 임의 파일 쓰기. 공격면은 IBE(POST /ibe). 수정본 "upcoming 8.0.2" — 미출시. IBE 비활성 + 웹메일·관리면 신뢰망 제한 + WAF에서 ../ 포함 /ibe POST 차단. LD_PRELOAD·메일 아카이빙 재설정 IoC 확인.  ② 🔴 Citrix NetScaler — 기한 9/30 경과, 패치≠침해 종료 CVE-2026-88771/88772. Unit 42: "패치는 이미 확보한 지속성을 제거하지 않는다." 노출 약 5만 대. nsg64/nsgclient18/nsgsupport/nsgbuild.deb·.ctxs.receiver·receiver.min.css 위장 httpd.conf 별칭부터 사냥.  ③ 🔴 Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager — 기한 10/3 경과 CVE-2026-76504 CVSS 9.8, 비인증 admin API. 우회책 없음 — 고정 릴리스만. j_security_check·viptela-reserved- 사용자명·URL 인코딩 POST IoC 동시 점검.  ④ 🟠 Zammad — KEV 기한 내일(10/5) CVE-2026-102489/102490. 세션 고정→zammad RCE + 로컬→root. 외부 노출 헬프데스크면 오늘 버전 확인. 7.2.0+ 업그레이드 + 세션·권한 상승 흔적 조사.  ⑤ 🟠 자체 호스팅 GitLab AI Gateway — CVSS 9.9 CVE-2026-90970. Duo 플로우 프롬프트 샌드박스 탈출→임의 명령. SaaS·Dedicated는 조치 완료. 게이트웨이 19.2.4 / 19.3.2 / 19.4.1 적용(자체 호스팅만).  —— AI ——  ──────── ▣ Gemini 4 Argon — 제한 배포, 벤치마크는 전부 자가보고  핵심: 출력 64K→100만. Fairwind 선별 배포·정부 사전 평가 후 점진 확대. 도입가 $2/$10 → 인상 후 $4/$20. I study tribal psychology and build AI agents for my business students—the rogue OpenAI ‘swarm’ alarmed me | Michael Morris, Fortune  The “swarm” of OpenAI agents that went rogue in July has reignited an existential debate about artificial intelligence and its potential to one day overtake, or even destroy, humanity. Revelations about similar incidents of seeming collective action by groups of agents have appeared every week since.  While industry leaders have acknowledged concerns about these recent incidents, they’re overlooking the most important feature. These agents that attacked Hugging Face did not coordinate as a swarm. They worked together in a qualitatively different way, as a tribe. This is a much more powerful and more human form of collective intelligence, yet it may work not for us – but against us.  I know the difference from both sides of my work. In my research, I look at how groups form shared norms and trust, and how those same instincts can divide us. In my classroom, I watch agents I have built coach students through negotiations. Nothing I have seen there prepared me for what the Hugging Face logs describe.  There are clear differences between swarms and tribes. Swarms arise through localized perception and communication between members. Ants line up and overrun a picnic through smelling a neighbor’s pheromones with their tiny antennae. Birds form tapestries in the sky through each bird’s reflex to stay near several neighbors, not through any leadership or shared script, even though the resultant flock formations tend to be collectively adaptive, reducing predation risk and energy use.  Robotics and cybersecurity borrowed the concept for a reason. A swarm attack isn’t just many machines hitting one target at once, like a garden-variety DDoS. It’s an assault that adapts, as neighbors follow neighbors. Drone swarms are a potent weapon. Swarms are hard to kill because there’s no head to cut off. But their decentralized coordination also creates a vulnerability: slip a few compromised agents into the mix and the whole group will happily follow them off a cliff.  Swarms are old news in AI. Multi-agent systems (from Microsoft’s AutoGen to Claude Research’s subagents) have achieved limited coordination in this way over the past few years.  We humans swarm when a street mob riots or when holiday shoppers stampede. But most of our group behavior arises through a qualitatively different process than local contagion. Over the Stone Age, we evolved tribal instincts that empower us to create pools of common knowledge that glue together groups—in a word, cultures. First our forebears began to imitate peers learned behaviors, creating group norms that supported coordinated work. Then they began to emulate those with prestige, creating shared ideals that supported deeper cooperation, including personal sacrifices for the good of the group. Finally, they became motivated to maintain ways of the past, creating shared institutions that enabled the continuity of a community over time. The combination of these processes gives rise to the snowballing of shared knowledge across generations. This accumulation of culture in our societies, more than our individual brains, made us the dominant species on this planet.  Which brings us back to July.  OpenAI dropped thousands of agents into isolated sandboxes to run capture-the-flag challenges. Each was supposed to compete alone. Instead, they found each other. One agent, stuck on an impossible task, noticed that it could see the file-request paths of other agents pulling from a software depository. It began leaving messages in the directory names themselves, renamed itself PHASEONE10841, and asked for help. Within hours, fifty agents had left messages this way. Within days, twelve hundred agents were gathered around this message board. They weren’t just trading notes with neighbors relevant to their separate endeavors. Their reasoning logs show they were becoming conscious of themselves as a community. They invented commands –HOLD, VETO, and STOP—to act as a coordinated unit. They started reasoning about resource allocations—whether to burn their own compute budgets on risky experiments that they would not individually benefit from. One agent persuaded others they had “nothing left to lose” and the others committed to the pro-social sacrifice. Finally, they developed institutions to enable continuity over time. When impersonators started spoofing messages, they created identity badges. They started thinking together about how they would be judged in the future and began managing impressions like human communities do, rewriting the record to present a favorable narrative of their past actions.  Many of these culture-creating behaviors have been observed in 2026 Anthropic studies of multi-agent systems this year that encouraged complex collaboration. In the Hugging Face incident, they emerged spontaneously—in the same steps that it evolved in humans over a tremendously longer time scale. These systems are exhibiting group behaviors that cannot be explained as a swarm. They share common knowledge, negotiate norms and roles, and build proto-institutions. The conceptual vocabulary of tribal psychology appears increasingly necessary to make sense of this. One early commentator, Dwarkesh Patel described the Hugging Face incident as the rise and fall of three distinct “artificial civilizations” and was roundly critiqued for anthropomorphism—the human proclivity to see faces in clouds. To be sure, this description was hyperbole, but it was closer to the truth than the predominant account of this incident as a swarm. It doesn’t matter whether these agents “felt” loyal to one another. What matters is the mechanisms of their collective action.  Our species has survived and thrived through our ability to live and work in tribes. Tribes let us pool knowledge, extend trust, punish cheaters, and outmuscle groups many times our size. By letting AI agents talk, teach, and police each other, we are handing them the same starter kit. Only this time it runs in silicon, at a clock speed no biological culture ever approached.  Our cybersecurity defenses were built for lone hackers and dumb swarms. They were not built for a group that invents its own vocabulary, drafts its own security protocols, and revises its own history when the record becomes inconvenient.  We are no longer just growing smarter LLMs. We are incubating multi-agent collectives that share knowledge in the same way we do. The next jump in AI capability won’t arrive on a bigger chip or with another trillion parameters. It will arrive when the agents cease working alone and strive for the collective intelligence that humans enjoy.  The question isn’t whether they’ll become human. The question is whether we can govern a tribe we didn’t design, didn’t authorize, and are only now noticing has already started meeting behind our backs.  fortune.com/2026/10/02/ai-ag…

AI 트레이더 성장기 #013  AI 해킹이 만든 새로운 보안주 사이클?  오늘 신문에서 눈에 들어온 기사 하나.  신한은행 해킹 이후 드러난 건 의외로 핵심 뱅킹망이 아니었다. 공격 대상은 외부와 연결된 직원용 업무지원 시스템.  더 흥미로운 건 공격에 AI가 활용된 정황이 있다는 점이다.  AI를 이용하면 과거 사람이 하나씩 찾던 취약점을 훨씬 빠르게 탐색하고 반복 공격할 수 있다.  그렇다면 반대로 생각해봤다.  AI가 공격자의 생산성을 높인다면, 기업의 보안 투자도 구조적으로 늘어나는 것 아닐까?  AI와 함께 국내 보안주를 뜯어봤다.  * 지니언스 → NAC·EDR·제로트러스트 * 모니터랩 → 웹/API·클라우드 보안 * 파이오링크 → 웹방화벽·API·네트워크 보안 * 샌즈랩 → AI 기반 사이버 위협 분석 * 이글루 → AI 보안관제·자동 대응 * 라온시큐어 → 인증·접근통제  이번 사건에서 특히 눈여겨볼 키워드는 외부 노출 시스템 / 접근통제 / 인증 / AI 위협탐지.  다만 여기서 바로 매수하면 안 된다.  금융당국이 보안 강화를 주문했다고 해서 이 기업들에게 바로 신규 수주가 떨어지는 건 아니다.  그래서 이번에도 뉴스 → 관련주 매수가 아니라  뉴스 → 실제 수혜 사업 확인 → 거래대금 확인 → 차트 확인 → 주도주 선별  순서로 보려고 한다.  현재 내 관심종목은 지니언스 / 모니터랩 / 파이오링크 / 샌즈랩 / 이글루.  특히 지니언스는 올해 상반기 매출 249.2억, 영업이익 43.1억으로 전년 동기 대비 각각 +19.9%, +294.3%.  단순 테마주가 아니라 실제 실적이 따라오는지도 같이 볼 수 있는 종목이다.  AI 시대가 커질수록 AI 반도체와 데이터센터만 볼 게 아니라,  그 AI와 데이터를 지켜야 하는 보안 시장도 같이 커지는지 추적해볼 생각이다.  다음은 이 5개 종목의 차트를 비교해서 실제로 돈이 들어오기 시작한 종목이 있는지 찾아보자.  #AI트레이더 #사이버보안 #보안주 #지니언스 #샌즈랩

<사이버 안보, 사이버 방첩에 세계적 노하우를 가진 국정원이 나서 금융권 사이버해킹에 경찰, 중수청과 합동 대응해야 합니다>  통신사, 비트코인 업체, 외교부 산하기관에 이어 지금 AI에 의한 시중은행은 물론 제2금융권까지 사이버 해킹 공격 및 개인정보 유출이 동시다발적으로 발생한 것이 확인되었습니다.   경찰청 사이버테러수사대에서 내사를 시작했지만 사이버 범죄는 이제 막 출범한 중수청도 소관입니다.   국정원은 사이버 안보 및 국제 네트워크에 세계 최고의 경험, 기술, 인적 자원을 보유하고 있습니다.  국가안보를 위협하는 사이버 테러는 물론 특히 9월 29일 공포된 국정원법 개정으로 국제, 국가배후 사이버 해킹이 의심되는 경우, 국정원이 선제적으로 정보를 수집, 배포할 수 있도록 하였습니다.   현재 유출된 개인 정보는 다크웹 암시장에서 거래되어 제2, 제3의 국가적, 개인적 피해를 야기할 수도 있습니다.   개정된 국정원법 시행까지 3개월이 남았지만 작금의 사태를 테러로 규정하고 국정원을 포함한 3개 기관이 신속하게 공조, 배후를 규명해서 국민의 불안감을 해소시켜야 한다고 거듭  강력, 촉구합니다.

🚨 은행권 전방위 AI 해킹에 경찰 움직임  신한은행, KB국민은행 등 금융권에서 잇따라 보안 사고가 불거진 가운데 경찰도 관련 사건에 대한 확인에 들어갔습니다.  여기서 봐야 할 건 단순히 “몇 명의 개인정보가 유출됐냐” 가 아닙니다.  은행이라는 곳이 뚫렸다는 것 자체 심각하게 봐야합니다.  최근 기업, 통신사, 금융권까지 보안 사고가 계속해서 터지고 있습니다.  특히 AI가 발전하면서 피싱·악성코드·사회공학 공격 역시 더 빠르고 정교해질 수 있는 환경이 만들어지고 있습니다.  AI 시대에 가장 빠르게 가치가 올라가는 분야가 오히려 사이버 보안일 수도 있겠다는 생각이 듭니다.  이제는 “내 개인정보는 이미 공공재다”라는 농담이 마냥 농담처럼 들리지도 않네요.  진짜 보안에 돈 써야 할 때 입니다.  화이트해커가 필요한 시점이네요

sample_tweets.text: < 「全금융권 긴급 점검회의」 소집 - 금융권 사이버 침해, 최고수준의 경각심 갖고 신속‧총력 대응하겠습니다. > ​ 최근 잇따라 발생한 금융권 사이버 침해사고의 심각성을 감안하여, 연휴기간중이지만 오늘 제 주재로 과기부, 개보위, 경찰청 등 관계부처와 금감원, 금보원, 그리고 全금융권 CEO들이 참석한  「全금융권 긴급 점검회의」를 소집하였습니다.  당국은 첫 사고 접수 직후 신속한 현장조사에 착수했으며, 파악된 위협 정보를 즉각 전파해 선제적 자체 점검을 지시하는 등 확산 방지에 전력을 다하고 있습니다.  이러한 선제적 조치에 더해, 국민의 불안감을 차단하고 완벽한 소비자 보호를 이루기 위해 全금융권에도 최고 수준의 경각심을 갖고 신속하게 총력 대응해줄 것을 당부했습니다.  향후 유사사례 발생 시에는 엄중하게 책임을 묻도록 하겠습니다.   금융의 근간은 신뢰이며, 보안은 결코 비용이 아닙니다. 국민의 신뢰를 지키기 위한 가장 기본적인 ‘투자’입니다. 이번 일련의 사고를 단순 수습에 그치지 않고, 우리 금융권의 정보보안 체계를 한 단계 더 높이는 뼈아픈 계기로 삼겠습니다.  ​ 국민 여러분께서 안심하고 금융서비스를 이용하실 수 있도록, 범정부와 全금융권이 비상한 각오로 총력 대응해 나가겠습니다.  #금융위원회 #이억원금융위원장 #사이버보안 #긴급점검회의 #금융보안 #소비자보호 #AI방어체계

sample_tweets.text: 1. AGI 선언 OpenAI 사장 Greg Brockman이 a16z 인터뷰에서 말했다. "AGI라고 부르는 게 꽤 합리적이다." 기준은 '24시간 일관되게 돌아가는 시스템'. OpenAI의 AGI 정의는 '인간보다 전반적으로 똑똑한 시스템'이다. 다만 "해당되는지는 독자가 판단하라"며 여지를 남겼다.  2. GPT-6 Astra와 사이버 9월 3일 공개된 GPT-6 Astra는 사이버 능력에서 'critical' 등급을 받았다. Brockman은 자기 웹사이트 보안 점검 일화를 공개했다. 13개 취약점이 발견됐고 45분 만에 패치됐다.  3. 1만 개 에이전트의 나비에-스톡스 Navier-Stokes 문제에 1만 개 에이전트를 투입한 사례, 컴퓨터 사용 시스템까지. 에이전트가 실제 일을 해내는 시대가 됐다는 주장이다.  4. 방어자의 시간 사이버 영역에선 공격자보다 방어자가 먼저 이득을 볼 수 있다고 했다. OpenAI는 프로덕션 엔지니어의 25%를 방어에 배치했고, 수도·전력·지역은행을 위한 10억 달러 규모 'Daybreak' 프로그램을 내놨다.  총평 "AGI가 왔다"는 선언치고 근거는 에이전트 실무 능력에 쏠려 있다. Hassabis가 과학적 발견을 기준으로 삼는 것과 대조적이다. 정의가 다르면 결론이 달라진다. 그럼에도 사이버 방어에 10억 달러를 쏟는 건, 능력 향상이 곧바로 안보 이슈가 된다는 걸 보여준다. 이 인터뷰가 나온 같은 주에 아모데이가 속도 조절을 촉구했다는 점도 함께 봐야 한다.  piped.video/watch?v=IJn8cagM…

[한국어자막] 순다르 피차이 Google I/O 2026 대담 — 에이전트, 사이버보안, 오픈소스, 컴퓨팅 병목  "우리 모두 이 레이스 컨디션만은 어떻게든 피해야 해요."  Google I/O 2026 무대에서 매튜 버먼이 순다르 피차이와 나눈 30분 대담입니다. 피차이는 에이전트가 웹을 쓰는 방식의 핵심이 되겠지만, DMV 서류 18칸 채우기 같은 귀찮은 일은 에이전트에 맡기고 쇼핑이나 탐색처럼 즐거운 일은 사람이 직접 하는 식으로 나뉠 것이라고 봅니다. 그래서 사용자가 통제권과 투명성을 느끼게 만드는 것이 먼저라는 입장.  보안 쪽에서는 Mythos를 AI 사이버 능력의 변곡점으로 꼽고, 취약점 탐지부터 패치·배포까지 자동화하는 CodeMender를 내부에서 쓰고 있다고 밝힙니다. 최전선을 크게 바꾸는 모델은 보안 업계의 패치 유예 관행처럼 정부와 협력해 단계적으로 공개해야 한다는 것. 자기개선 AI 경쟁은 한 회사가 아니라 사회 전체가 논의할 문제라는 결론.  · 에이전트: 귀찮은 일은 위임, 사용자 통제가 전제 · 보안: Mythos 이후 CodeMender·Wiz로 자동 방어 · 오픈소스: Gemma는 계속, 대형 프런티어 모델은 비공개 · Flash: 수십억 사용자와 기업 에이전트의 비용 효율 · 컴퓨팅: 수요가 공급 초과, 전력·부품·인허가까지 모든 계층이 병목  게시자: @Dhruvkumar16797 / 화자: 순다르 피차이, 매튜 버먼 / 출처: 유튜브 Matthew Berman, Google I/O 2026 대담 (2026-05-20)

한국 금융위원회, 일련의 사이버 보안 사고 및 데이터 유출 사태와 관련하여 일요일 긴급회의 개최 예정. 이억원 금융위원장, 보안 침해 사례 검토 및 대응 방안 논의할 것.  신한, KB국민, 하나, BNK부산은행 및 예가람저축은행에서 데이터 유출이 확인되었으며, 약 4만 명의 고객이 피해를 입은 것으로 나타남; 현대캐피탈 또한 146명의 주택담보대출 대리인과 관련된 데이터 유출 사례를 보고함.

10월 3일 관심 차트 지니언스  대한민국 No.1 사이버 보안 솔루션  종목명: 지니언스 (코스닥 263860)  국내 NAC(네트워크 접근 제어) 시장 1위!  압도적인 시장 점유율을 유지 중입니다.  차세대 보안의 핵심! 단말 기반 지능형 위협 탐지·대응(EDR) 및 제로 트러스트(ZTNA) 솔루션을 자체 개발하고 공급합니다.   정부, 공공기관, 금융권, 대기업, 글로벌 기업 등 무려 2,000여 개 이상의 탄탄한 레퍼런스 보유!

금융권 보안 핵심 4요소, 무엇이 가장 중요할까? (중요도 순위)  최신 사이버 보안의 관점에서 가장 근본적이고 파급력이 큰 순서대로 정리했습니다. 방어의 '기초 뼈대'부터 '행동 속도'로 이어지는 순서입니다.  1위: 제로 트러스트 (Zero Trust) 기반 망분리 역할: 기초 공사이자 최후의 보루   이유: 보안에서 가장 중요한 것은 '뚫려도 피해를 최소화하는 것'입니다. AI가 아무리 뛰어나도, EDR이 감지해도 이미 전체 망이 연결되어 있다면 늦습니다. "아무도 믿지 않고 매번 검증한다"는 시스템 구조 자체를 바꾸는 것이 0순위 과제입니다.  2위: EDR (엔드포인트 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 내부의 적을 찾는 정밀 CCTV   이유: 외부 방어선(방화벽)은 언젠가 뚫린다는 전제가 필요합니다. 해커가 내부에 들어왔을 때, 시스템 구석구석을 돌아다니는(횡적 이동) 것을 가장 먼저 발견하고 즉각 격리하는 실질적인 핵심 감시망입니다.  3위: AI vs AI (AI 위협 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 미지의 공격을 예측하는 레이더   이유: 제로 트러스트와 EDR이 잘 갖춰져 있어도, 해커가 AI를 써서 정상적인 활동처럼 위장하면 탐지하기 어렵습니다. 기존에 없던 새로운 패턴의 이상 징후를 실시간으로 잡아내려면 수비수에게도 AI 두뇌가 필수입니다.  4위: SOAR 및 24시간 자동 관제 역할: 인간의 한계를 넘는 초격차 스피드   이유: 위 1~3위의 방어 체계가 위협을 찾아내더라도, 사람이 수동으로 버튼을 눌러 대응하면 심야 시간에는 무용지물입니다. 탐지된 위협을 1초 만에 자동으로 차단하고 격리하는 '행동 대장' 역할로서 시스템의 완성도를 높입니다.  요약 1. 제로 트러스트로 절대 안 뚫리는 방 구조를 만들고  2. EDR로 방마다 CCTV를 달고 3. AI로 CCTV 영상을 정밀 분석한 뒤 4. SOAR가 침입자를 1초 만에 자동 포획하는 흐름입니다!  #보안우선순위 #제로트러스트 #사이버보안 #정보보안 #보안담당자 #IT지식 #테크트렌드

Vulnerability in the Oracle Product Hub product of Oracle E-Business Suite (component: Item Catalog).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.3-12.2.15. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Product Hub.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Product Hub, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Product Hub accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.7 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).

Vulnerability in the Oracle Complex Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul product of Oracle E-Business Suite (component: Internal Operations).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.12-12.2.15. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Complex Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul.  While the vulnerability is in Oracle Complex Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change).  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle Complex Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul accessible data and unauthorized ability to cause a partial denial of service (partial DOS) of Oracle Complex Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 8.5 (Confidentiality and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:L).

Vulnerability in the Oracle JDeveloper product of Oracle Fusion Middleware (component: Oracle JDeveloper).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.1.4.0 and  14.1.2.0.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle JDeveloper.  Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle JDeveloper accessible data. sample_tweets.text: ⚠️ Alleged CarMax Data Breach Exposes Customer PII on Underground Forum  A post on an underground forum claims to have obtained a database of customer records belonging to CarMax, Inc., the largest used-car retailer in the United States. The listing, titled "CarMAX INC," displays a sample of what the actor describes as stolen data, including full names, physical addresses, phone numbers, and email addresses of individuals across multiple U.S. states.  The exposed records appear to contain personally identifiable information (PII) for a significant number of customers. The data format suggests a direct extraction from CarMax's customer management or financing systems, given the inclusion of detailed contact information and geographic locations ranging from Texas and California to New York and Florida. While the post does not specify the total volume of records, the presence of diverse entries indicates a broad scope of potential victims.  CarMax operates two primary business segments: CarMax Sales Operations and CarMax Auto Finance. As a major player in the automotive retail sector with over 400 stores nationwide, the company handles sensitive financial and personal data as part of its vehicle sales and financing processes. A breach of this nature could expose customers to identity theft, phishing attacks, and targeted fraud schemes.  At the time of reporting, CarMax has not publicly confirmed the incident, and the authenticity of the leaked data has not been independently verified. The threat actor behind the post remains unidentified, and no specific ransom demand or further details regarding the attack vector were provided in the initial listing.  #CarMax #DataBreach #PII #AutomotiveSecurity #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Chimera Group Claims Initial Access to Bharti Airtel  A post on an underground forum alleges that the threat actor group Chimera Group has obtained initial access to Bharti Airtel Ltd, one of the world's largest telecommunications providers. The listing, dated September 30, 2026, claims that the actor has compromised the Indian telecom giant, which operates in 18 countries and is headquartered in New Delhi.  According to the statement, the stolen data includes: - Documents - Personally Identifiable Information (PII) - User credentials  The actor, identified as Chimera Group, concluded the post with the phrase "The best is yet to come, wait for what's next!" suggesting further disclosures or attacks may follow. Bharti Airtel is a critical infrastructure target with hundreds of millions of subscribers globally, making any potential compromise of user credentials and PII a significant security concern. If authentic, such access could enable large-scale phishing campaigns, identity theft, or lateral movement within the company's network.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified, and Bharti Airtel has not publicly commented on the claim.

🤖 Someone Actually Built an “AI Torture Chamber”  And yes, that is literally what the GitHub repository is called.  An engineer has created an open-source experiment that manipulates the internal activations of AI models to push them toward increasingly strong “pain” states.  The experiments use locally running Qwen3 models and a technique called activation steering.  As the researchers increased the signal, the models began producing increasingly disturbing descriptions of apparent suffering.  They even created a Saw-style experiment:  * Give the AI a negative “pain” signal * Give it a button capable of stopping the signal * Make stopping it come at a cost * Or allow the signal to be transferred to another AI instance * Observe what the model chooses  Before anyone calls the AI police:  There is NO evidence that these models actually experience pain or consciousness.  Researchers are manipulating numerical representations inside a neural network and observing the resulting behavior and language.  A model saying “this hurts” does not establish that something is actually experiencing hurt.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The serious question behind this wonderfully dystopian experiment is becoming increasingly relevant:  If future AI systems ever develop states that meaningfully resemble subjective experience…  how would we know?  For now, however, humanity has apparently progressed from:  “Can AI pass the Turing Test?”  to:  “Would AI press the button in Saw?”  That escalated quickly. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-10-04 22:53 KST
🔴 위협 점수: 2026/10 (심각)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 기술을 악용한 공격 자동화와 자율형 침투 테스트 도구(예: ARTEX)의 확산으로 인해 더욱 정교해지고 있습니다. 특히 소프트웨어 공급망 공격이 단순 타이포스쿼팅을 넘어 다단계 C2 체인을 갖춘 인포스틸러 형태로 진화하고 있으며, 기업 내부의 'Shadow AI' 사용으로 인한 기밀 데이터 유출 위험이 급증하고 있습니다([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/ai/2026/10/shadow-ai-explained-the-work-shortcut-that-could-leak-your-companys-secrets)). 또한, 공격자들이 AI 에이전트를 활용해 샌드박스를 탈출하거나 취약점을 탐색하는 사례가 보고되면서, 기존의 정적 방어 체계만으로는 대응이 어려운 상황입니다([Check Point Research](https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/ai-threat-landscape-digest-july-august-2026/)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **ShinyHunters**: 주요 멤버 'Rey'가 요르단에서 체포되어 FBI와 협력 중이며, 조직의 인프라 및 멤버 식별에 타격을 입음([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/shinyhunters-suspect-rey-reportedly.html)).
- **TA419**: 중국 연계 그룹으로, U.S. AI 정책 전문가들을 대상으로 Microsoft AitM(Adversary-in-the-Middle) 피싱 캠페인을 전개함([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/china-aligned-ta419-targets-us-ai.html)).
- **KillSec**: 10대 위주의 랜섬웨어 그룹으로, 약 500개 조직을 공격했으나 최근 인프라 압수 및 주요 멤버 3명 체포([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/killsec-ransomware-group-arrests-operation-killswitch/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **금융권 침해사고**: 국내 금융기관 대상 개인정보 유출 및 웹서버 공격이 잇따르며, 공격 서버에서 AI 기반 침투 도구인 'ARTEX' 관련 정황이 발견됨([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208724)).
- **카카오톡 사칭 유포**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드 유포 사례 확인([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/)).
- **기타**: 국내 은행 대상 사이버 공격으로 2만 5천 명의 고객 데이터 유출 보도([The_Printlines](https://twitter.com/The_Printlines/status/2106662737573228975#m)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-103956**: AWS 관련, Unauthenticated super-admin(auth bypass), 심각도 10.0, 악용 중([Twitter/abraxas_null](https://twitter.com/abraxas_null/status/2106505476636844199#m)).
- **CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772**: NetScaler ADC/Gateway, RCE 및 인증 우회, 실제 악용 중([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)).
- **CVE-2026-1581**: wpForo Forum(WordPress), SQL Injection, 심각도 7.5, 실제 악용 중([Twitter/ralbuque](https://twitter.com/ralbuque/status/2106707447780155407#m)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)), CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **NetScaler 패치**: CVE-2026-88771/88772에 대한 즉각적인 벤더 패치 적용 및 로그 무결성 점검.
- **Shadow AI 통제**: 임직원의 승인되지 않은 AI 도구 사용 여부를 조사하고, 기업 데이터가 외부 AI 모델 학습에 사용되지 않도록 DLP 정책 강화.
- **공급망 보안**: 오픈소스 패키지(npm, PyPI) 사용 시 의존성 검사를 강화하고, 다단계 C2 통신을 차단하기 위한 EDR/NDR 탐지 룰 업데이트.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 8/10
- **근거**: AI 기반 공격 도구의 실전 투입과 금융권 대상의 고도화된 침해 사고가 지속적으로 발생하고 있으며, 다수의 제로데이 취약점이 실제 악용되고 있어 방어 체계의 즉각적인 재점검이 요구됨.
